notes: First promotion from the new legal and civil society lane (probe of 21 July 2026): a legal challenge to NRW's own permitting practice that no government source would ever surface. Genuinely two-way for SI4, hence neutral: a ruling against NRW could force wider assessment of off-site nutrient pollution (tightening the regime the indicator depends on) while creating capacity and casework pressure; a ruling for NRW entrenches the current boundary interpretation that campaigners argue leaks pollution. Either way the scope of agricultural permitting in Wales is being tested in court. Watch for the permission decision and any hearing date, and set event_horizon when one is fixed.
summary: River Action has launched a judicial review of NRW's approval of permit variations allowing three intensive poultry units in Powys to expand (reported 17 February 2026). The claim argues NRW unlawfully treats the site boundary as the boundary of its regulatory responsibility, and that under the Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016 the regulator must assess and control pollution impacts from permitted activities including manure exported off site. Outcome pending.
title: River Action takes NRW to judicial review over Powys poultry permit variations; scope of off-site pollution responsibility contested
